items.title: Code-Based Apple-Style Keynote Motion Design Prompt
items.summary: A creator shares a concise prompt used with Opus 5.5 to generate a dynamic 15-second motion graphics video.
items.prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a one-word brand name for the wordmark (a verb works best), 9 to 12 high-res photos, a royalty-free song around 120 BPM with a drop and a quiet breakdown (Mixkit, free for commercial use), and a free stock clip of a plain wall with moving plant shadows (Pexels).
</inputs>

<direction>
An Apple-keynote launch film, 2D only, one continuous take. Every scene is made out of the previous one: nothing fades, blurs or cuts. Objects change shape instead: text rises out of a mask line, icons pop from zero on a spring, bars draw across, pages push, and a black shape floods the whole frame and contracts into the next scene. Warm off-white canvas, black UI, iOS 26 liquid glass over the photos. Archivo (wdth 125, weight 800) for the wordmark, Geist for UI. A cursor drives every change with real clicks, drags and long-presses. The camera zooms screen-studio style so each moment fills the square, and the cursor scales with it.
Banned: crossfades, blur-ins, brightness "developing", 3D flips, particles, glows, holds longer than 1s, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 54 beats, something happens on every beat.
Open: the wordmark squeezes into its own period like an accordion, the dot grows into a black pill, a label rises inside it. Click: six iris blades close over the label and snap open onto a photo. The circle becomes a square, shrinks, the grid unfolds from behind it like a paper map (center, plus, corners), reflows into a bento, and a click zooms into one tile, landing exactly on the drop.
Glass: a glass word pops in letter by letter, melts into a droplet that stretches into a glass toolbar. The adjust icon turns it into a slider. Dragging relights the photo from day to golden hour (two aligned shots), and the knob turns into a glass lens while held. It lifts into a glass orb, the next photo opens inside it as a circle, and the orb expands into a lock screen: glass clock digits, date, and a home bar that stretches into a glass music player.
Stage: the lock screen pulls back into a phone (the bezel grows out of the screen edge). The Dynamic Island stretches like liquid, pinches off, flies over and grows into a Mac window that rolls up like a blind. Long-press the wallpaper, drag it onto a Safari tab, the page pushes in, drop it and it becomes the hero of a landing page. Scroll: the hero morphs into a framed print on a product card, with the mat and molding growing out of the photo's edge. Pick a frame color (it paints across) and a size, then the nav button flies down into "Order print".
Order: one black shape keeps morphing: Ordered ✓ → Printing % → On its way (a van on a route) → Delivered ✓.
Wall: the delivered circle floods the frame edge to edge, holds black for a beat, and contracts into the framed print hanging on the real wall footage. The same iris opens onto the print, closes again, the frame floods the screen and contracts into the pill → the dot → the letters spring back out, landing on the beat return. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is computed from time inside an async seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state between frames.
2. Springs are closed-form step responses. A value with many targets is the sum of one spring per change, so it stays a pure function of time.
3. Liquid glass: each glass element holds its own clone of the scene behind it, filtered with an SVG feImage displacement map (a rounded-rect distance field) through three feDisplacementMaps at slightly different scales for chromatic edges, plus a rim light. Glass letters: a canvas distance field per glyph gives the map, mask and highlights.
4. Goo: blur + alpha threshold, then composite the source atop it so the glass stays sharp inside.
5. Iris: 6 blades around a hexagonal aperture. Each blade is its two vertices, both edge extensions and the SHORT arc between them.
6. Wordmark squeeze: every letter moves toward the dot by the same factor and its drawn width follows (narrow the wdth axis, scale the rest), so the letters stay touching.
7. Footage: re-encode all-intra (ffmpeg -g 1), load it as a blob URL, await 'seeked' before drawing each frame.
8. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event (Mixkit), never synthesized, each placed by its measured peak. The song starts on a downbeat: the zoom lands on the drop, the wall sits in the breakdown, the wordmark returns with the beat. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
9. Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame blended with ffmpeg tmix, 60fps. Check one frame per beat, then scan for single-frame pops (frame-difference spikes 3x their neighbours).
</build>

<gotchas>
backdrop-filter: url() misreads displacement maps in Chromium, so clone the scene instead. A flood must overscale past the corners and take about 0.3s, or half the screen changes in one frame. A child with visibility: visible shows through a hidden parent, so use inherit. Text that swaps inside a morphing shape needs its own mask. python http.server can't range-seek video, so use the blob URL.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 4 stills (open, glass, stage, wall) before you write the full film.
</start>

  - 0:04–0:06.5 — Multimodal: One continuous stream transforms into text, waveform, image frame, and video timeline.

  - 0:06.5–0:09 — Agents and tools: The stream branches into sandboxed agent runs, then reaches external tools

  - 0:09–0:11.5 — Reliability: An interrupted stream freezes, reconnects, and resumes from the same point; a clean

  - 0:11.5–0:15 — Reveal: All paths converge into a bold final composition: “TanStack AI” followed by “Build what’s

  to read it.

items.title: Minecraft-Style Browser Sandbox Game Prompt
items.summary: Game / playable prototype
items.prompt: Build a browser sandbox game in the spirit of Minecraft that feels as close to the original as possible. All in-game text in English. Controls: keyboard and mouse (desktop).  TECH - A single HTML file, plain WebGL2, no third-party libraries. - All 16×16 textures generated in code as pixel art (stone, dirt, grass, planks, leaves, ores, glass, water, lava, etc.). - Sounds synthesized with WebAudio: digging, footsteps, placing blocks, damage, mobs, explosions, calm background music.  WORLD - Infinite world made of 16×16×128 chunks, with a seed. - Biomes: plains, forest, birch forest, taiga, snowy tundra, desert, mountains, oceans, beaches. - Caves (winding tunnels and large caverns), lava at the lower levels, ores by depth: coal, iron, gold, diamonds. - Three tree types, tall grass, flowers, cacti, sugar cane, pumpkins. - Minecraft-style lighting: sky light and block light (torches, glowstone, lava) that spreads cell by cell, with smooth lighting and ambient occlusion. - Day/night cycle: sun, moon, stars, sunsets, 3D clouds, distance fog, rain. - Water and lava flow by levels; two sources make infinite water; water + lava make obsidian or cobblestone. Sand and gravel fall.  PLAYER - First person, collisions, jumping, sprinting, sneaking (doesn't fall off edges), swimming, ladders, fall damage. - Block breaking with crack stages and particles; break time depends on the tool. - Visible hand and held item with a swing animation. Third-person view on F5.  SURVIVAL - Health, hunger, saturation, air underwater. - Tools in 5 materials with durability, armor in 4 materials. - Inventory with 2×2 crafting, 3×3 crafting table, furnace with fuel, chests, bed (skip the night and set spawn). - Item drops, death and respawn. - Mobs: pigs, cows, sheep, chickens (breeding, shearing); at night zombies, skeletons with bows, spiders. Zombies and skeletons burn in sunlight. - Farming: hoe, seeds, wheat growth, bread. Doors, fences, fence gates, TNT.  CREATIVE - Flying on double-tap Space, instant block breaking, a catalog of all blocks with tabs and search.  UI - Title screen with a world panorama, world list (create / delete / play), options (FOV, render distance, sensitivity, sound, brightness, GUI scale). - Pause menu, death screen, HUD (hotbar, hearts, hunger, armor, air bubbles), F3 debug screen. - Chat with commands: /gamemode, /time, /give, /tp, /summon, /weather. - Worlds saved in localStorage.  RESTRICTIONS - Do not use Minecraft's name, logo, textures or characters (Steve, Creeper, etc.): give the game its own name and design your own mobs.  TESTING - Run the game in a headless browser, check every system and fix bugs before delivering.

items.summary: EDteam Promotional Motion Graphics
items.prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: my product name, a logo (or let you draw a simple mark), my brand colours (or pull them from my logo), the one-line thing a user types into the prompt box, the page that answers it (title + 2–3 sentences with one key phrase), two feature names for the stacked cards, and a music track. If I skip any, use the defaults: product "Frame by Frame" living inside its Whop hub, a viewfinder mark (four corner brackets around a bold "FF"), prompt "Make a launch video for my app", a lesson page titled "2.1 Choose a reference", cards "Launch" and "Sound", and Mixkit's free house track "Rising Forest" slowed to 124 BPM.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 12 second square product sting, 1080x1080, frame numbers at 29.97 fps (f0–f359), master rendered at 59.94 fps. Apple-keynote feel: soft, white, bright blue, glassy. The camera never cuts on a still frame: every shot enters already moving (exponential ease-out, 12–19% of the remaining distance per frame) and leaves on an accelerating move or a blur ramp. Blur follows speed and direction on every move.
Palette: my brand colours mapped onto these roles; if I give none, use page #FDFDFB, haze #B7CFEB, ice #E6F0FA, deep blue #294376 → #769CC2 sky gradient, navy #1E2F52, accent blues #2F6BFF / #3CC8F0 / mint #4ED6A0, white. Type: Inter (400/500/600/700). No purple, violet, magenta or orange anywhere.
Story: the product header rises out of a blue haze inside a light app window → a cursor glides in, turns to face where it's going, grows on hover and clicks the logo → hard cut on the music drop to the app icon with four squares orbiting into a cross → the icon collapses into a Mac menu bar → the cursor clicks the menu-bar icon, a frosted glass prompt box springs out and the prompt types → whip-tilt up through a light-blue flash into the answer page scrolling into place → a card rises over it → blur-dissolve to two stacked cards with giant frosted-glass titles → blur-dissolve to the lone logo disc → hard cut to a black end card with a glowing wordmark.
Banned: crossfades, frozen frames (except one hold in S7), stock UI kits, glows on UI text, Math.random, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
Coordinates are px on the 1080 stage. Music beat k = 0.048 + 0.4838·k s (124 BPM, one beat = 14.5 frames). The three hard cuts f72, f101, f159 land 2 frames before a beat: keep these exact frames.
S1 f0–71, header + window + click: haze #B7CFEB fading to #FDFDFB by f28, keep a blue floor glow #DBEEFD at the bottom. Header on one line: logo disc ⌀132 (#FBFCFE, 1px rim #E8E8EA, dark mark), the product name (Inter 500), a dark capsule pill "on Whop" (#2F2E2F, white text); the whole lockup spans x474–1063, centre line rises y932 (f0) → 776 (f2) → 683 (f5) → 608 (f10) → 546 (f24) → 536 (f37), drifting 1 px/frame after. 1. One HTML page, 1080x1080, drawn by seek(t) as a pure function of the frame number. No CSS transitions, no timers, no Math.random (seeded hashes only). Shots register as {f0, f1, render(localFrame)}.
2. Every value is continuous in the frame number (the 59.94 master renders half frames): animate with keyframe tables kf(frame, [[f, value], ...], ease) and per-frame lookup tables with linear interpolation. No Math.floor on motion.
3. Blur: CSS filter blur for round blur, SVG feGaussianBlur with separate x/y stdDeviation for directional smears. Zoom smear on the end card = 20–30 scaled, faded copies of the word. Frosted glass = a blurred, lightened copy of what's behind, clipped to the shape.

Master to −14 LUFS, true peak −1 dBTP, no fade except the last 60 ms.
6. Render with Playwright (one screenshot per frame, fonts loaded first), encode H.264 yuv420p at 60000/1001, mux the audio.
</build>

<gotchas>
Measure text only after the fonts load. A long product name won't fit where a 5-letter name did: scale the whole lockup (disc gap, name, pill) to fit the span x474–1063, don't let the pill fall off-frame. Keep the cut frames exact even where they don't sit on a beat. Nothing freezes except S7 f269–287. Heavy blur tables can wipe a shape out completely: if a frame looks empty, lower the blur until the shape still reads.
</gotchas>

items.prompt:
Create “Melon Jelly” - a polished, interactive 3D watermelon jelly slice that runs directly in the browser using genuine WebGPU and WGSL shaders.
Deliver a single, self-contained HTML file with embedded JavaScript and CSS. This must be an actual interactive 3D simulation, not a static render, video, or 2D imitation.
THE WATERMELON
Create a thick, rounded triangular watermelon wedge with:
Translucent ruby-red jelly flesh.
A pale, slightly translucent layer between the flesh and rind.
A glossy green outer rind with irregular dark-green stripes.

Individually modeled dark seeds embedded in both exposed sides.
Softly rounded corners and an appealing, substantial thickness.
Make it look like an expensive gummy candy photographed in a studio. It should feel juicy, soft, and almost edible. Keep the colors rich without overexposing the highlights.
SOFT-BODY PHYSICS
Use a volumetric soft-body simulation, such as a tetrahedral mesh with XPBD elastic and volume-preservation constraints.
The user must be able to:
Grab the tip, a corner, the flesh, or the rind.
Stretch, bend, lift, and gently twist the slice.

Release it and watch it wobble before gradually settling.
The slice must visibly deform locally, not simply move or scale as one rigid object. Make the rind slightly firmer than the flesh while keeping the whole slice flexible.
Preserve volume reasonably during stretching. Prevent inverted elements, explosive motion, and permanent collapse. Use a fixed simulation timestep and bounded substeps for stability.
After release, the motion should decay naturally - no instant snapping back and no endless oscillation.
Keep seeds attached to the deforming flesh. They must move and rotate with the surface rather than float independently or remain fixed in space.
Include ground contact, gentle friction, and soft bouncing. Avoid visible floor penetration.
RENDERING
Use native WebGPU with WGSL shaders.
Include:
Thickness-dependent light absorption.
Refraction through the jelly.

Fresnel reflections and glossy highlights.
Soft transmitted light through thin edges.
Subtle internal details and a few tiny air bubbles.

Soft contact shadows beneath the slice.
A light, neutral studio background.
The flesh, pale rind, and green skin should have distinct material responses. Avoid making everything look like clear glass or opaque plastic.
Keep the slice large and easy to inspect, with a three-quarter camera angle that reveals the flesh, seeds, and thickness.
INTERFACE
Use a minimal editorial layout with generous whitespace, thin borders, restrained controls, and no decorative UI gradients.
Top left:
“MATERIAL STUDIES / NO. 009”
A large italic serif heading split across two lines: “Melon” and “Jelly.”
Small caption:
“A slice of summer.”
“A little wobble.”
“Too soft to share.”
Top right:
A small status indicator showing “WEBGPU · LIVE” when the renderer is running.

Right-side panel:
“THE SPECIMEN”
Three coordinated watermelon-inspired color presets.
Firmness slider with its current value.
Internal damping slider with its current value.
“Give it a nudge” and “Reset” buttons.
“¼ speed” and “Show mesh” checkboxes.

Pause / Resume button.
Bottom left:
A short hint explaining that the slice can be grabbed and stretched.
Live mass, relative volume, and kinetic-energy readouts derived from the simulation. Clearly describe illustrative units or approximate values where appropriate.
Bottom right:

A collapsible “Inside the experiment” section briefly explaining the physics and rendering.
BEHAVIOR AND PERFORMANCE
Support both mouse and touch input. Use pointer capture so dragging remains reliable when the pointer leaves the object.
Make the layout work on desktop and mobile without controls covering the slice.
Reuse buffers and avoid rebuilding geometry or compiling shaders during dragging. Keep interaction smooth and responsive.
Respect reduced-motion preferences. If WebGPU is unavailable, display a clear explanation instead of silently substituting a fake renderer.
VALIDATION
Test dragging from several locations, strong stretches, repeated releases, ground collisions, all sliders, presets, pause, reset, and slow motion.
Check that the model returns to a stable resting shape, seeds stay attached, the mesh remains intact, and there are no rendering errors.
Prioritize the quality of the jelly response and lighting. The result should be something people want to keep grabbing and playing with.

items.title: Interactive WebGPU Strawberry Cake Soft-Body Physics
items.summary: Claude Opus 5.5 generated a self-contained WebGPU/XPBD soft-body 3D watermelon jelly simulation shown in a side-by-side screen recording.
items.prompt:
Build immediately a complete interactive WebGPU site called “Strawberry Cake.” 
Use genuine WebGPU + WGSL, procedural geometry, mouse/touch, and real-time volumetric soft-body physics. No Three.js/Babylon.js, Canvas2D, external assets, video/GIF, or CSS-only deformation.
Visual: premium Korean/Japanese strawberry shortcake—low, wide, rounded, pillow-soft, with pink sponge, cream layers, pale frosting, piped cream, and strawberries. Warm ivory background, soft studio light, edible moist materials.
Layout: top-left “SOFT STUDIES / NO.001” + italic “Strawberry Cake.” Top-right “WEBGPU · LIVE”. Large centered cake. Right controls: Hand/Knife, presets, Firmness, Damping, Drop, Reset, Pause, ¼ speed, Show mesh. Bottom-left: Mass, Volume, Kinetic, Pieces.
Physics: stable XPBD/co-rotational soft body with tetrahedral sim mesh, smooth render mesh, volume preservation, damping, gravity, floor friction, and piece collisions. Cake feels soft/heavy and wobbles after release.
Hand: hold=Press, inward drag=Squeeze, outward drag=Grab, fast release=Throw. Use weighted grabs, smoothed 3D target, pointer velocity and momentum. Cake remains free; cake input overrides orbit.
Knife: procedural 3D knife. Draw a cut line; animate contact→compression→penetration→breakthrough→lift. Deform before splitting; keep seam thin.
Repeated cutting is mandatory: use a dynamic pieces list; every piece stays cuttable. Convert strokes to vertical cut planes, split crossed pieces, create new soft-body/render meshes, transfer deformation/velocity, preserve toppings, keep halves aligned, update Pieces. Support 14+ pieces and multi-piece cuts. No fixed whole/left/right states.
Drop releases all pieces. Reset restores one intact cake and Pieces=1. Use fixed timestep/substeps, DPR≤2, clamp instability, avoid NaNs/GPU errors. Expose window.__cake.
Run locally, test interactions and repeated cutting, and iterate until polished.

items.title: Fictional Fashion Commercial Direction with Claude Opus 5.5 and MiniMax H3
items.summary: Motion graphics / showreel
items.prompt:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the model in <Picture 1>, including their face, skin tone, hairstyle, hair color, body proportions, and outfit exactly as shown.
<Subject 2> is the wearable product in <Picture 2>, including its exact silhouette, proportions, colors, materials, surface finish, and any printed label or logo design exactly as they appear in the image.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video is a 15-second cinematic fashion commercial in which <Subject 1> wears <Subject 2>. It is built as eight 1.5-second scenes followed by a 3-second hero finale. Each scene changes location, lighting, and composition on the beat, and in each scene one short word exists physically inside the environment. The finale is a full-frame hero shot in front of giant illuminated letters spelling "QUIVRE", with the tagline "Carry your own light." and the call to action "SHOP NOW".

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 2], [Shot 4], [Shot 5], [Shot 6], [Shot 7], [Shot 8], [Shot 9]): fully_preserved - the face, skin tone, hairstyle, hair color, body proportions, and outfit from <Picture 1> stay identical throughout; if <Subject 2> is a clothing item, footwear, or accessory, it replaces only the matching item of that outfit.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1] to [Shot 9]): fully_preserved - the shape, proportions, colors, materials, surface finish, and logo from <Picture 2> stay identical in every shot.

detailed_description:
The target video is a photoreal cinematic fashion commercial shot at blue hour and night, with low-key lighting, strong backlight and rim light, drifting atmospheric haze, wet reflective surfaces, deep contrast, and a color scheme of cool steel-blue shadows against the warm glow of <Subject 2>'s own dominant color. <Subject 1> is the only person, and <Subject 2> is the only featured product, worn naturally and always clearly visible and in focus. Every word of text exists physically inside the scene and is spelled exactly as written; it never covers the face or the product, and no other text appears.
[Shot 1] Total darkness filled with slow-moving haze. A narrow horizontal blade of white light sweeps across the frame and projects the word "QUIVRE" in thin, widely spaced capital letters onto a dark concrete wall. As the blade passes, it catches <Subject 2> worn by <Subject 1> in the foreground in a tight close-up, rim-lighting its edges and igniting its warm color. The camera pushes in slowly. A deep bass hit lands with the light sweep.
[Shot 2] At 00:01.500, the shot cuts to a long concrete tunnel at blue hour with a blinding white backlight at its far end and haze in the air. <Subject 1>, wearing <Subject 2>, walks out of the backlight from silhouette toward the camera, passing between enormous freestanding concrete letters spelling "NEW" that stand on both sides of the path. The camera tracks backward at a low angle. Heavy footsteps echo.
[Shot 3] At 00:03.000, the shot cuts to an extreme macro of <Subject 2> on the body of <Subject 1> in a dark room. A hard spotlight passes through a metal stencil and casts the word "DETAIL" as sharp letter-shaped light onto the dark wall behind, while the camera glides across the product's material texture and edges in raking light.
[Shot 4] At 00:04.500, the shot cuts to a windswept rooftop at dusk under a deep blue sky. Behind <Subject 1>, a huge white fabric banner printed with the black word "FREE" billows and snaps violently in the wind. Their hair whips across their face as they turn back toward the camera, <Subject 2> clearly visible. The camera circles at a low angle. Wind roars and fabric cracks.
[Shot 5] At 00:06.000, the shot cuts to a rain-soaked city crosswalk at night. Large white road-painted letters reading "EVERY DAY" lie across the wet asphalt, glistening with reflected streetlights and blurred traffic lights. <Subject 1> strides across the letters while the camera tracks alongside at the height of <Subject 2>, the painted words sliding through the foreground. Water splashes softly under each step.
[Shot 6] At 00:07.500, the shot cuts to a tall glass wall in a dark modern building lit by cold blue light from outside. The word "LIGHT" is etched large into the glass in the foreground. Behind the glass, <Subject 1> walks from left to right with <Subject 2> visible through the clear parts of the glass, their figure passing behind the etched letters. The camera slides sideways, creating strong parallax between the letters and the model.
[Shot 7] At 00:09.000, the shot cuts to a dark studio with haze. Enormous three-dimensional letters spelling "BOLD" stand behind <Subject 1>, sculpted from the same material and color as <Subject 2> and lit by one hard top light that throws deep shadows. <Subject 1> holds a still, confident full-body pose in front of them, wearing <Subject 2> on the body exactly as in the other shots; <Subject 2> is large, sharply lit, and never hidden or left out. The camera snap-zooms in on the beat. A punchy whoosh-and-hit accent lands.
[Shot 8] At 00:10.500, the shot cuts to a close-up of <Subject 1>'s face together with <Subject 2> beside a night window. Outside, a warm illuminated sign spelling "YOURS" is reflected in the window glass next to their face, blurred by raindrops. <Subject 1> looks directly into the camera with a calm, confident expression. The camera pushes in very slowly. Rain taps softly on the glass.
[Shot 9] At 00:12.000, the shot cuts to a newly staged, full-frame wide shot of a vast dark studio that fills the entire frame edge to edge, with no black bars, borders, or framed picture. Giant freestanding illuminated letters spelling "QUIVRE" glow warm white across the back of the set, reflected on the glossy black floor. <Subject 1> stands slightly right of center, large in the frame from head to knees and filling about two-thirds of the frame height, in a composed hero pose while wearing <Subject 2>, which is sharply lit by a spotlight and clearly readable as the hero product. In the empty lower-left area of the frame, clean white text "Carry your own light." fades in, then "SHOP NOW" appears inside a thin rounded outline button beneath it, never over the model's body. The camera stays locked off with no zoom or push-in so the whole face always stays in frame, and the final half second holds completely still like a printed advertising key visual. A final bass hit rings out with a long shimmering tail.

overall_soundscape:
Cinematic, close foley throughout, with whooshes on every cut and a low room hum under the finale. No voices or narration.

non_diegetic_music:
A dark, stylish electronic track at about 80 BPM with a deep sub-bass, a hard kick and snap, metallic percussion, and tense pulsing synths. Every cut lands on every second beat. It builds from [Shot 4], peaks at [Shot 7], then drops to silence for a breath before a final huge bass hit at 00:12.000 and a long reverb tail.

items.title: Opus 5.5 Motion Designer Showreel
items.summary: Motion Graphics Showreel
items.prompt:
Make a 15-second motion-design showreel, like a résumé portfolio reel for a motion designer named CLAUDE. Go all out.
- 1920×1080, 60 fps, exactly 15 s. Every frame and every sound is generated in code.
- 128 BPM, 8 bars; each section is one bar (1.875 s), and every move lands on a beat.
- Palette: ink #0C0C10, bone #F2EEE6, red #FF3B1D, cobalt #2E4BFF, lime #D8FF3C. Fonts: Bahnschrift (variable), Noto Sans TC, Consolas.
- A red dot is the recurring hero and ends as the period in "CLAUDE."
Sections: 00 dot bounces with squash & stretch → stretches into a line that splits the screen ·
01 kinetic type MOTION / DESIGN (spring mask, red bar wipe, variable-weight ripple, marquee, push into the "O") ·
02 17×9 shape grid (radial waves: circle → square → Truchet arcs → spiral collapse) ·
03 GLSL-raymarched red blob (sphere → metaballs → torus → twist → squash) ·
04 drop: 26k particles, curl-noise flow → form 動態設計 → gust ·
05 8 rapid cuts, one per half beat (data viz, glitch, UI, line art, halftone, isometric, radial, ridgelines) ·
06 3×3 grid of live tiles → shuffle → zoom into the center ·
07 CLAUDE bursts from the dot, the dot lands as the period, "MOTION DESIGNER / 動態設計師", "AVAILABLE FOR NEW PROJECTS".
HUD with timecode and beat meter, adaptive motion blur, shake + flash on impacts, grain.
Synthesized soundtrack in F minor (Tone.js), drop at 7.5 s, −14 LUFS.
Build as a seekable renderFrame(f) HTML page, rendered with Playwright + ffmpeg.

items.title: Squid Jelly: Interactive 3D WebGPU Gummy Squid Simulation
items.summary: Procedural Rube Goldberg Machine in Blender
items.prompt:
Create “Squid Jelly” — a beautiful, interactive 3D gummy squid that users can grab, stretch, and squish directly in their browser. Deliver a complete standalone HTML file using genuine WebGPU.

ART DIRECTION

Make the squid look like a premium translucent gummy candy:
- An elongated, tapered mantle with a rounded tip.
- Two broad, thin, diamond-shaped side fins.
- Eight shorter curled arms and two longer feeding tentacles with rounded club-shaped tips.
- Small suction cups and a cute, understated face.

Use a warm off-white background, soft studio lighting, and a subtle ground shadow. Keep the squid large and centered, with an elegant, uncluttered composition.

GEOMETRY

Generate all geometry procedurally. No external models or image files.

Connect the arms, tentacles, and fins smoothly to the body. Their roots must remain embedded and attached during strong pulls, with no visible gaps or floating parts.

Suction cups and eyes must follow the deforming surface. Give the fins a thin, flexible profile and the longer tentacles slender shafts with thicker tips.

JELLY MATERIAL

Create convincing glossy, translucent jelly:
- Thickness-dependent color absorption.
- Refraction and soft internal light scattering.
- Smooth studio reflections and delicate rim highlights.
- A few tiny bubbles embedded inside the material.
- Richer color in thick areas and greater translucency along thin fins and tentacle tips.

Avoid opaque plastic, washed-out colors, blown-out highlights, visible mesh seams, and flickering transparency.

SOFT-BODY PHYSICS

Use a stable mass-spring or position-based dynamics simulation with approximate volume preservation.

The mantle should feel soft but substantial. Arms should bend independently, while long tentacles and fins should be more flexible.

Let users grab the body, fins, or tentacles at the clicked location. Pulling must deform the nearby geometry first, with the rest following elastically. Do not fake softness by scaling or rotating the entire model.

On release, the squid should wobble, recover its shape, and gradually settle. Include gravity, floor collisions, friction, and damping. Prevent appendages from passing through the floor.

Use fixed simulation steps, bounded stretching, and robust attachment constraints so repeated strong pulls cannot tear the model apart or destabilize the simulation.

INTERACTION

- Left-click or touch the squid to grab and stretch it.
- Right-drag or drag empty space to gently orbit the camera.
- Support limited zoom and mobile touch controls.
- Keep camera gestures separate from object dragging.

Add:
- Give it a nudge
- Reset
- Reset view
- Pause
- Firmness slider
- Internal damping slider
- ¼ speed toggle
- Show mesh toggle

Provide three material palettes: Coral, Lagoon, and Grape. Switching colors must not reset the simulation.

INTERFACE

Use a minimal editorial layout:
- Top left: small “MATERIAL STUDIES” label.
- Large italic serif heading: “Squid Jelly.”
- Caption: “A little ink. A little wiggle. A very sweet sea creature.”
- Top right: WebGPU status indicator.
- Right side: compact “THE SPECIMEN” control panel.
- Bottom left: a short interaction hint.

Use clean sans-serif controls, thin borders, and generous whitespace. Adapt the layout for mobile without covering the squid.

QUALITY AND PERFORMANCE

Use real 3D geometry and native WebGPU rendering with WGSL shaders, not a 2D imitation or prerecorded animation.

Reuse meshes and buffers. Do not reconstruct geometry during dragging. Prioritize stable interactions and smooth performance.

Test strong pulls, repeated releases, appendage attachments, floor collisions, palette changes, pause, reset, and camera controls.

Provide a clear fallback message if WebGPU is unavailable.

Deliver the full working HTML, not a mockup or code fragment. The result should feel like a little living gummy toy: glossy, weighty, flexible, and irresistibly satisfying to stretch.

~150-second, fully automated, cinematic camera journey "inside the mind of
an AI". Render everything through a custom ASCII post-processing shader
(dense monospace glyph grid, characters chosen by luminance, tinted per
scene, subtle glow and film grain). No cuts — one continuous camera path
with smooth crossfades between rooms.

Scenes (in order, each with its own palette):
1. Black void with sparse drifting glyphs. Center terminal prompt "> wake _"
   with an orange (#D97757) chevron and blinking cursor.
2. Amber/gold infinite library hall — tall shelves, arches, glowing lamp,
   camera dollies forward.
3. Teal/blue towering pillars made of falling digits.
4. Purple constellation: floating words connected by lines, forming a web.
5. Grey staircase climbing upward into darkness.
6. Deep red room of noise with a single lit doorway; camera approaches it.
7. Pale/warm room where a calm face made of characters emerges.

Captions: bottom-center, lowercase, JetBrains Mono, letter-spaced, on a
soft dark gradient bar. Each line types in with a "decode" effect (random
glyphs in orange resolve into the real letters). Use this script, timed
across the scenes: [paste the captions above]

Make the timeline deterministic (driven by a time variable, not real
time) and expose window.renderFrame(t) so it can be captured frame by frame
at 1920x1080, 30fps. Add a ?record flag that hides the UI.

the rest is fine tuning the room until it looked all good

items.summary: AI Consciousness ASCII Journey
items.prompt:
SCENE CONTEXT
Chaotic amateur first-person phone footage shot by a standing passenger during rush hour inside a packed magnetic-levitation train that races through one violent, unbroken 30-second journey with no cuts.
The video begins immediately inside a colossal titan valley. Enormous humanoid titans hundreds of meters tall are already walking beside and across the train route. The journey then flows continuously into a prehistoric dinosaur basin, through a gigantic living jungle, upward into a futuristic megastructure suspended across the sky, through an enormous machine-city built at impossible scale, and finally into a vast artificial world where entire cities surround a contained artificial sun.
The scale continuously escalates.
The car violently heaves, snakes, drops, and banks throughout the journey. Everyone inside is tightly packed and gripping poles or straps, enduring the ride almost silently.
The phone operator grips a pole with one hand and films shakily with the other, repeatedly swinging the phone between the crowded passengers and the left-side windows as unbelievable environments rush past.
A calm public-address voice bookends the journey.
LOCATION MAP
Interior foreground:
A standing-room-only futuristic maglev commuter car.
Bodies pressed shoulder to shoulder.
Passengers gripping overhead straps and vertical poles with white knuckles.
Backpacks squeezed between bodies.
Coats and loose clothing shifting with each jolt.
A narrow central aisle completely jammed with standing commuters.
Large panoramic windows run along the LEFT side of the carriage.
The camera remains inside this exact same train car for the entire video.
The train always travels in the SAME forward direction.
Everything outside streaks past the windows front-to-back.
Exterior zones crossed in this exact continuous order:
Colossal Titan Valley.
Prehistoric dinosaur basin.
Dense gigantic prehistoric jungle.
Ascending mountain passage leading into clouds.
Enormous futuristic ring megastructure above the clouds.
Interior machine-city of impossible scale.
Artificial-world civilization surrounding a contained miniature sun.
Each zone physically connects into the next.
No teleportation.
No instant environment replacement.
No discontinuity in geography.
Camera stays inside the car at chest height.
Exterior light enters primarily from the LEFT windows.
FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING
Open immediately on chaos.
At 0.0 seconds the phone is already recording.
The frame is crooked, off-center, and partially blocked by the shoulder of another standing passenger.
Foreground:
A commuter grips a vertical steel pole with both hands as the carriage violently sways.
Mid-ground:
Three passengers white-knuckle overhead straps.
Their bodies all lean simultaneously under a strong lateral force.
The camera swings unintentionally toward the LEFT windows.
Outside, before the first second is finished, an absolutely colossal humanoid titan is already walking beside the speeding train.
Only one leg, part of its hip, and the bottom of its torso can fit inside the phone frame.
Its upper body disappears far above the top of the window.
Another titan moves in the distant valley.
The nearby titan's enormous hand swings past the windows only several meters away, momentarily covering almost the entire sky.
Its footsteps hammer the landscape.
One foot lands beside the track.
The impact sends dust and small rocks outward.
The train violently jolts.
The phone rolls sideways from the force.
Instant hook.
No establishing delay.
FORMAT MODE
ONE CONTINUOUS SHOT.
The camera never cuts on its own.
There are NO hard cuts anywhere.
Every environment change happens naturally and physically as the train moves forward.
The same train interior remains visible throughout.
The same passengers remain in approximately the same positions.
The camera never exits the carriage.
No montage.
No invisible transition.
No teleporting.
No speed-ramp transition.
No black-frame transition.
No hidden cut behind objects.
Real-time throughout.
OPTICS
Single first-person consumer smartphone camera.
Wide 63° FOV held throughout.
Cheap modern phone-lens character.
Slight barrel distortion.
Soft mushy image toward the edges.
Very aggressive rolling-shutter jello during violent jolts.
Vertical structures bend briefly during fast pans.
Autofocus hunts whenever enormous creatures suddenly pass close to the glass.
Auto-exposure pumps strongly when moving between shadow, daylight, cloud, and artificial light.
Smeared realistic motion blur during rapid camera movement.
Occasional digital sharpening halos.
Compressed highlights.
Crushed shadows.
Low-bitrate macroblocking during darker moments.
Tiny greasy fingerprint streaks on portions of the lens.
No cinematic lens language.
No shallow depth-of-field beauty shots.
Everything feels captured accidentally on a passenger's phone.
CAMERA
Handheld phone at chest height.
One-handed filming.
POV belongs to a standing passenger who must use the other hand to grip a vertical pole.
The train continuously throws the operator off balance.
Sustained camera behavior:
sharp lateral whips,
violent short drops,
continuous low-frequency turbulence,
rolling horizon,
yawing frame,
small accidental zoom-like hand movement without actual digital zoom,
occasional shoulder obstruction,
brief thumb grazing one corner of the lens,
autofocus breathing,
exposure correction,
imperfect reframing,
moments where the camera points too low or too high before correcting.
Whenever something enormous appears outside, the operator instinctively tries to tilt the phone upward but can never fit the full scale inside the frame.
No stabilization.
No smooth gimbal movement.
No impossible camera orbit.
No exterior camera.
No drone shot.
No cinematic cutaway.
ACTION
0.0s to 5.0s — TITAN VALLEY
At exactly 0.0 seconds:
soft PA chime.
Calm public-address voice says exactly:
"Please remain inside the train."
Nothing else is spoken.
The phone is already pointed halfway toward the crowded aisle and halfway toward the LEFT windows.
Outside:
a massive open valley under harsh bright daylight.
Huge grass-covered ridges.
Rock formations.
Dust hanging in the distance.
Several colossal humanoid titans walk slowly through the valley.
They are hundreds of meters tall.
Grounded biological giants.
Not superheroes.
Not robots.
Not monsters with exaggerated fantasy powers.
Ancient weathered skin.
Heavy natural musculature.
Mineral-like stone growths across portions of shoulders and backs.
Vegetation growing naturally across some surfaces.
Cloud wisps around the tallest bodies.
A nearby titan walks parallel to the train.
Only fragments of its enormous body fit in frame.
At approximately 0.7 seconds its gigantic hand swings beside the carriage, filling almost the entire window.
Passengers instinctively lean away from the glass.
Nobody screams.
The titan's foot lands beside the track.
A huge pressure wave pushes dust and loose vegetation outward.
The train shakes brutally.
Overhead straps snap sideways.
The phone slams briefly into the operator's shoulder.
The camera recovers.
Ahead, another titan slowly steps across the valley.
Its leg crosses above the rail corridor.
The train races underneath its raised body.
Its shadow sweeps over the carriage.
The entire interior goes dark for less than one second.
Then sunlight returns.
The train continues forward without slowing.
5.0s to 10.0s — DINOSAUR BASIN
The rocky titan valley gradually becomes greener.
The titan silhouettes recede behind the train.
Ferns appear beside the track.
Low vegetation grows denser.
The terrain opens naturally into a huge prehistoric basin.
The phone presses close to the LEFT window.
A herd of horned dinosaurs suddenly appears running parallel to the train.
Dozens of animals.
Dust erupts beneath their feet.
Bodies jostle realistically within the herd.
Some animals briefly disappear behind others.
Their motion obeys weight and momentum.
The train keeps overtaking them.
A large dinosaur runs very close to the glass for a moment.
Its textured hide, blinking eye, and pumping muscles become visible before falling behind.
Ahead:
three enormous sauropods cross the basin.
Their scale dwarfs the herd.
The train passes beneath the neck of one.
The neck stretches across the sky like a moving bridge.
Then a gigantic sauropod foot lands near the track behind the train.
Impact.
Dust erupts.
Passengers are thrown sideways.
A loose backpack slides across the floor.
The phone operator nearly loses grip.
10.0s to 14.5s — PREHISTORIC JUNGLE
The open dinosaur basin narrows.
Huge trees begin appearing.
The train enters a dense prehistoric rainforest without any cut.
Massive trunks rise higher than buildings.
Broad leaves flash past the windows.
Branches pass dangerously close to the carriage.
Sunlight flickers rapidly through the canopy.
Several smaller feathered dinosaurs sprint through the vegetation beside the train.
One briefly jumps across a fallen tree.
Another turns its head toward the moving carriage.
Far deeper in the jungle, something much larger pushes through trees.
Branches snap.
Leaves shake.
The body itself remains partially obscured.
Then a gigantic predatory dinosaur breaks briefly into view on a parallel ridge.
Not directly attacking.
It runs through the jungle for several seconds, partially hidden by trees.
Its head flashes between trunks.
The operator tries to follow it with the phone.
Autofocus keeps snapping onto leaves in the foreground.
The train begins climbing.
The jungle floor drops away.
14.5s to 19.0s — ASCENT INTO THE CLOUDS
The train races out of the jungle onto a steep elevated rail wrapping around an enormous mountain face.
Prehistoric vegetation gradually thins.
Wind noise rises.
The valley now drops thousands of meters beneath the windows.
Tiny dinosaurs can still be seen far below.
The rail climbs aggressively upward.
Passengers lean backward under the incline.
The camera shakes harder.
Cloud begins flowing across the windows.
At first wisps.
Then dense white fog.
The exterior becomes almost completely white.
Only fragments of rail supports appear through the mist.
The train keeps climbing.
Light becomes brighter and more diffuse.
Auto-exposure begins clipping highlights.
Then the cloud layer suddenly thins naturally ahead.
The phone catches glimpses of something impossibly large through gaps in the cloud.
19.0s to 23.5s — FUTURISTIC SKY MEGASTRUCTURE
The train breaks above the cloud layer.
Reveal:
an incomprehensibly massive futuristic ring megastructure suspended above the clouds.
It stretches beyond the horizon in both directions.
Its scale is far larger than any building.
A whole civilization covers its surface.
Thousands of towers rise from the ring.
Gigantic bridges connect distant sections.
Transit lines wrap around the structure.
Massive rotating habitat sections move slowly.
Hundreds of distant trains race along curved rails.
Flying maintenance craft appear tiny against the structure.
The phone operator instinctively tilts upward.
The ring still cannot fit inside the frame.
The carriage receives intense white-blue daylight from the LEFT.
Passengers momentarily stop looking at their phones.
Several glance toward the windows in quiet disbelief.
The train's track curves directly toward a monumental rectangular opening in the side of the ring.
The opening itself is large enough to contain skyscrapers.
As the train approaches, the enormous structure blocks the sun.
The carriage gradually falls into shadow.
The train enters the opening.
23.5s to 27.0s — MACHINE CITY
Inside the structure:
a vast mechanical canyon.
The scale is impossible but physically grounded.
The train races between enormous industrial systems.
Building-sized gears rotate slowly beside the track.
Magnetic rings activate sequentially as the train passes.
Kilometer-tall elevator shafts move platforms vertically through the structure.
Gigantic maintenance arms slide along rails.
Massive rotating cylinders spin deep below.
Other maglev trains pass on distant tracks.
Tiny lights reveal entire neighborhoods built into the machine walls.
Large mechanical doors open ahead moments before the train reaches them.
Everything operates with tremendous weight.
No magical motion.
No floating pieces without visible structural support.
The machinery produces heavy vibration.
The train rattles continuously.
Blue-white industrial illumination sweeps across passengers as the carriage crosses repeated light bands.
A huge rotating mechanism moves overhead.
Its shadow slides across the entire car.
The phone rolls upward trying to follow it.
A magnetic pulse causes a hard low-frequency vibration through the carriage.
Autofocus briefly loses the scene.
Ahead:
an intensely bright circular opening appears.
The train races toward it.
27.0s to 30.0s — ARTIFICIAL SUN WORLD
The train exits the machine structure.
The phone sensor blows almost completely white for a fraction of a second.
Auto-exposure struggles.
Then detail gradually returns.
Reveal:
an enormous artificial world.
A cylindrical interior civilization stretches farther than visibility.
Cities cover gigantic curved surfaces above, below, and beside the train.
Gravity-defying-looking architecture is actually attached physically to the rotating cylindrical structure.
Thousands of towers.
Suspended bridges kilometers long.
Countless moving trains.
Tiny spacecraft traveling between layers.
Massive agricultural terraces.
Artificial oceans visible in distant curved sections.
At the center of the entire structure floats a contained miniature artificial sun.
It is surrounded by colossal magnetic containment rings.
Brilliant warm light floods the windows.
The camera tilts upward.
The scale remains impossible to fit inside frame.
Far beyond the miniature sun, an even larger dark structure slowly moves across part of the light.
Only a portion is visible.
Its true size cannot be understood.
Do not reveal what it is.
The train begins slowing for the first time.
At approximately 28.8 seconds:
soft PA chime.
The same calm announcer says exactly:
"Welcome to the next world."
The line ends cleanly before 30.0 seconds.
The passengers remain silent.
The train keeps moving forward.
End while still inside the same continuous shot.
PERFORMANCE
All passengers are ordinary weekday commuters.
Photoreal human detail:
natural pores,
subtle facial redness,
realistic eye moisture,
catchlights,
natural blinking,
small unconscious mouth movements,
real breathing,
slightly messy hair,
subtle sweat,
wrinkled everyday clothing.
The car is extremely packed.
Everyone must remain physically connected to their surroundings.
Hands stay wrapped around poles and straps.
Bodies sway together according to train acceleration.
Passengers bump shoulders naturally.
Weight shifts realistically through legs.
Faces remain mostly tired, blank, confused, or quietly curious.
No exaggerated Hollywood panic.
No screaming.
No dramatic pointing.
No cheering.
No synchronized reactions.
One child near the LEFT window displays the most visible curiosity.
Adults mostly endure the impossible journey like exhausted commuters.
During the largest shocks:
a few people flinch,
one person grabs a pole with a second hand,
someone braces against a neighboring shoulder,
a loose backpack slides,
one overhead strap swings violently.
Nobody falls unrealistically.
TITAN DESIGN
Titans must feel enormous because of scale, movement, atmosphere, and interaction with the landscape.
Do not make them generic monsters.
Grounded humanoid anatomy.
Extremely large.
Heavy.
Slow compared with the train.
Natural inertia.
Each step produces delayed environmental response:
ground compression,
dust displacement,
vegetation movement,
small rockfalls.
Their full bodies should rarely fit inside the phone frame.
Nearby titan body parts should move slowly relative to their immense scale.
No glowing eyes.
No laser attacks.
No magical energy.
No fire breath.
No superhero poses.

DINOSAUR DESIGN
Dinosaurs should be grounded, realistic prehistoric animals.

Realistic mass.
Modern paleontological detail where appropriate.
Subtle feathers only on suitable species.
No fantasy dinosaur armor.
No glowing markings.
No hybrid monsters.
Sauropods should feel enormous through partial framing.
Predatory dinosaur remains an animal, not a villain.
No attack on the train.
FUTURISTIC STRUCTURE DESIGN
Architecture must communicate enormous scale through repetition, atmospheric depth, tiny comparative objects, and physically plausible engineering.
Use:
gigantic structural ribs,
magnetic rail systems,
thick support beams,
rotating habitats,
bridges,
industrial mechanisms,
elevator shafts,
maintenance platforms,
dense distant lights,
tiny transport vehicles.
Avoid generic neon cyberpunk streets.
Avoid hologram clutter.
Avoid floating random geometry.
Avoid meaningless sci-fi shapes.

Continuous inertia.
Sharp lateral forces.
Short vertical drops.
Constant mechanical vibration.
Overhead straps swing according to acceleration.
Loose clothing follows momentum.
Bodies sway in the same direction before recovering.

Outside:

Dinosaur feet interact with mud, soil, and vegetation.

Huge animals move with believable inertia.
Tree branches bend and snap naturally.
Cloud flows around structures.

LIGHTING
0.0–5.0s:
Strong natural daylight in Titan Valley.

5.0–10.0s:

AUDIO
NO MUSIC.

Cheap phone microphone.

OUTPUT SETTINGS

items.prompt:
Make a 30s 16:9 video (1920×1080, 30 fps) in HyperFrames (npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes), with voiceover, matching the quality standards below.

## REQUEST
- Topic: Polymarket gives 84% chance to Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 runoff (10/25).
- Positive focus on Flávio across four points: 1. the market that predicted Trump in 2024 points to Flávio; 2. first-round polls favored Lula, but Flávio won; 3. Flávio got 5 million more votes than his father in 2022; 4. Lula's administration banned Polymarket in Brazil.
- CTA: Share so more people see the facts.
- Destination: X and LinkedIn.

## FACTS
- Polymarket, 10/06/2026: Flávio 84.2% vs Lula 15.5%, $174M volume.
- US 2024: Polymarket had Trump 58.1% vs Harris 41.9%.
- Round 1 2026 Polls vs TSE Result: Flávio 47.03% (56,104,503) vs Lula 45.16%.
- Ban: CMN Res 5,298/2026.

## RULES
- Betting odds are not election polls; label accordingly.
- Display 'AI generated voiceover' badge.
- Free-license Wikimedia photos only.

## SCRIPT
[dramatically] O mercado que acertou o Trump dá oitenta e quatro por cento pro Flávio. [serious] No primeiro turno, cinco de seis institutos davam Lula na frente. [dramatically] Deu Flávio. Cinquenta e seis milhões de votos. Cinco milhões a mais que o pai em vinte e dois. [serious] E quem proibiu o Polymarket no Brasil? O governo Lula. Não é pesquisa. É dinheiro de verdade. [dramatically] Compartilhe. Mais gente precisa ver os fatos.

## VOICE
- ElevenLabs eleven_v4, voice 'Randel - Deep Epic'. Align cuts to Whisper timestamps.

## SCENES
0. Cover (0-1s): Flávio photo, Polymarket 84% text.
1. Trump portrait, 58% badge.
2. Counter 0->84%.
3. Polls paper graphic.
4. TSE result.
5. Vote comparison bar charts.
6. Planalto Palace and ban decree.
7. Stock exchange background.
8. Street crowd and share CTA.

## VISUAL DIRECTION
- Palette: #100F0D bg, Newsreader and IBM Plex Mono typography, Ken Burns pan effects, GSAP timeline.

## AUDIO
- ElevenLabs music prompt, SFX on cuts, master -14 LUFS.

## DELIVERABLE
Save polymarket-flavio-30s-horizontal.mp4.

items.title: Night Monster
items.summary: Procedural 3D Character Animation
items.prompt: The humanoid face in the mirror, monster, woman, hands, facial close-ups, and bathroom all adopt the same distinct AAA computer-generated fantasy game CG aesthetic; the woman must also possess the sculpted facial volumes, strand-bundled hair, and unified material shading of a polished game character, preventing her from looking like a live-action actor while only the monster is CG. Not live-action footage, cosplay, standard gameplay, 2D animation, or cel-shaded. The image natively fills the entire widescreen; no text, subtitles, titles, logos, or watermarks throughout. Environment: late night in an old, cramped bathroom with low ceilings, yellowed and cracked white square tiled walls, and dark weathered floor tiles; an old rectangular mirror hangs on the wall above the sink, its edges marked by black oxidation spots; below the mirror is a white ceramic sink and a narrow countertop. The only noticeable practical light source is a white candle placed on the right side of the sink counter, its flame flickering continuously, casting warm amber light from below onto the subjects and throwing thick but readable elongated shadows; a light mist lingers in the air after a bath. Maintain desaturated brown, dark gold, and monster reddish-brown palette without cold blue neon or modern lighting. Exactly two independent subjects: A is an adult female approximately thirty years old, fair skin, medium build, wet dark brown long hair draped over her shoulders, wearing a dark grey long-sleeve pajama top and dark trousers, unarmed. She stands before the sink facing the mirror, shoulders stiff with terror, hands braced on the sink rim, wide-eyed, breathing rapidly. B is the same giant, slender humanoid monster: initially disguised as A's reflection in the mirror—sharing an identical face, wet hair, and pajamas, but smiling while A is not, with the mouth corners barely wider than normal and eyes slightly more open, expression quiet, stiff, and unnatural, not a cartoonish grin. Once peeled open, the interior reveals a deformed elongated face of interwoven dark red and fleshy-pink muscle bundles, sunken nasal cavities, staring round eyes, fine ivory teeth, and an abnormally stretched oral cavity with multiple rows of teeth aligned longitudinally down the oral cavity and deep into the lower jaw; the mouth is a tall, narrow vertical slit whose height greatly exceeds its width when open, not a round hole or skull-like; the head, neck, and torso maintain continuous anatomical structure, not several distinct heads. The entire body consists of sculpted reddish-brown and fleshy-pink biological tissue with defined contours across shoulder blades, spine, ribs, elongated arms, and thighs, with restrained wet highlights, not a human painted red. Limbs are extremely long, hands thick with slender fingers, standard two arms and two legs; no armor, weapons, horns, wings, or visible genitalia. When crawling out of the mirror and crouching, it remains significantly taller than A, forced to bend knees and hips and lower its back under the low ceiling; scale disparity is communicated through the woman, sink, candle, and mirror together. The humanoid reflection and subsequent red behemoth represent the continuous state of B shedding its disguise, with no third subject added. 0.00–0.60s: Begin directly with a tight frontal close-up of the mirror reflection, face filling the frame from forehead to chin with mirror oxidation spots faintly visible at the borders; wet hair clings to the face, illuminated from below by candlelight, background blurred. Reflection stares straight into the camera with that stiff, unnervingly subtle smile; camera nearly static with a minimal slow push-in, without first establishing an empty bathroom. 0.60–3.10s: Retain the full-frame frontal close-up; one hand of the reflection grasps the top hairline while the other pinches the lower edge of the chin; hands only grip the perimeter, never obscuring the central face, eyes, or mouth. Upper hand pulls upward, lower hand pulls downward, peeling the humanoid face open along a straight vertical midline. Fingers gain purchase, outer layer tightens, then pale skin splits down the center revealing the continuous red monster face beneath; fine moist connective fibers stretch across the fissure. Fingers consistently hold the same outer layer without introducing a separate face or flashing into a monster. Movement is slow, continuous, showing tensile resistance; camera does not cut away from the reveal. 3.10–4.90s: Continue the close-up; the peeled halves remain attached at the sides of the head without falling off, each human eye still open and staring directly into the camera; the elongated red monster face pushes forward between them into full view, displaying both remaining human eyes alongside the monster face. It parts the tall, narrow vertical slit revealing rows of fine teeth and stretched jaw anatomy, uttering a low, non-verbal hiss; moist fibers tauten and slacken between the face halves and red flesh. Maintain visceral body-horror reveal without fire, lightning, transformation beams, or duplicated heads. 4.90–7.20s: Hard cut to a frontal close-up of woman A from the mirror's perspective at a slightly low angle. She freezes at the sink, eyes wide, brow furrowed, mouth slightly parted in terror, chin trembling, head pulling back slightly; wet hair and pajama collar sharp, one side lit by candlelight while the other falls into shadow. Continuous breathing and micro-reactions without speaking. 7.20–10.90s: Maintaining A's framing, two massive reddish-brown monster hands reach out from the mirror into frame: the mirror surface ripples and yields like liquid black mercury as arms push through. One hand presses onto her forehead and hairline while the other cradles her jaw, long fingers depressing the lower lip. Clear contact between palms, forehead, and jaw is established before opposing force gradually forces her head backward and mouth open wider. Her eyes remain locked on the creature in the mirror, throat straining, hands gripping the sink rim tightly; contact remains clear without covering her eyes or clipping through cheeks. Her face remains identical, only opening wider under supernatural pressure without mutating. 10.90–13.40s: Hard cut to a low-angle side wide shot establishing bathroom geometry: A stands at the left before the sink, head forced back; mirror and sink on the right wall. B has crawled more than halfway out of the undulating liquid mirror: long arms stretch left holding her forehead and jaw; torso hunched over the sink, one long leg stepping out with foot planted on the counter rim, other leg trailing in the rippling glass, knees bent and back arched under the low ceiling. Candle sits secure on the counter's right beside the monster's foot. B tilts head back, opening the narrow vertical slit to maximum revealing multiple tooth tiers, releasing a raspy, piercing non-verbal screech vibrating through throat and chest, making the candle flame flutter violently. 13.40–17.00s: Continuing the side wide shot, B keeps mouth agape after the screech, lowering head and neck toward the front-left, aligning its elongated face toward A's unnaturally opened mouth; the stabilizing hand on her forehead and supporting hand on her jaw sustain the posture as the monster's head begins continuous descent into her mouth opening. A remains braced at the sink, torso arched back, hands gripping the edge, neck taut. B's head and neck make contact and gradually enter, keeping massive back and hindquarters outside; does not engulf A into the monster's mouth, no inverted orientation, no transparent mesh clipping. 17.00–20.00s: Persisting wide shot, B's shoulders push forward-left, neck and head increasingly obscured within A's oral cavity, massive arched back shifting weight as the second leg steps out onto the counter, mirror surface behind settling back to calm reflection of the dim room. Both hands firmly hold forehead and jaw without extraneous limbs; A trembles with weakening knees but remains upright, pajamas creasing under tension. Candle remains standing, flame wavering, shadows of creature and woman shifting slowly against the tiles. Ends at 20 seconds amidst ongoing intrusion with bulk and legs still outside, without concluding full penetration, escape, transformation, or death. Rhythm & Cinematography: Slow-burn supernatural horror reveal without devolving into chase or melee. Preserves shot progression: reflection close-up peel — woman's reaction close-up — hands emerging to manipulate jaw — side wide shot showing massive scale crawling out, screeching, and descending. Driven by continuous deformation and reaction, settling into a sustained wide shot for full spatial dynamics; avoids orbit shots, abrupt zooms, unrelated reaction cutaways, or jumpscare black frames. Slowness derives from calculated force and approach, without artificial ultra-slow motion, speed ramping, or freezes. Consistent warm amber grade, candle lighting direction, and spatial continuity. Continuity: Exactly two subjects; A remains adult female, wet brown hair, dark grey pajamas at the same sink; B has two arms and two legs, with the peeled reflection face identical in material and anatomy to the emerged giant body. Mirror remains unbroken without glass shards. Intact anatomy throughout, clear hand placement, entry trajectory strictly monster head into woman's mouth. Emphasizes bio-mechanical forms, dread reactions, and progressive uncanny action without gore splatters, flying viscera, or dismemberment. Strictly prohibits background music: no score, soundtrack, melodic themes, rhythmic percussion, choir, songs, musical drones, or tonal ambience at any point. Only synchronized diegetic audio native to the physical scene: slow sink drip, faint candle crackle, subtle tile resonance, fabric friction, woman's breath and strained gasps, monster's low breathing, wet tearing sound of parting tissue, low liquid resonance of distorted mirror, skin contact sounds, the raspy piercing screech from 10.90–13.40s, and deep creaks of strained joints. No dialogue, voiceover, intelligible speech, or subtitles; no musical cues or rhythmic pulses filling silence. Any presence of background music fails evaluation. music=0; no_music=1; strict_no_music=1; audio=diegetic_only; Native full-bleed frame without letterboxing, rounded corners, text, subtitles, titles, logos, UI, or watermarks.
items.author: MadMax_Series

items.title: Interactive 3D Coral Reef Diorama Simulation
items.summary: 3D Spaceport Digital Twin Dashboard
items.prompt:
Build "Coral Reef", a playable miniature-diorama world: a glass aquarium block of tropical sea where the player brings a bleached coral reef back to life, as ONE self-contained HTML file.

It must be **beautiful above everything**, like a premium animated film: a jewel-like aquarium with crystal-clear water, dancing light, saturated coral colours and lively, characterful fish. Great animation on everything that moves: nothing pops, snaps or teleports; things grow, ease, overshoot a little and settle. Calm and satisfying to play, spectacular to watch.

## Tech

* three.js r170 with WebGPURenderer (automatic WebGL2 fallback). Load it with an importmap from jsDelivr: map "three", "three/webgpu" and "three/tsl" to `three@0.170.0/build/three.webgpu.min.js`, and "three/addons/" to `three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/`.
* Use TSL node materials, OrbitControls from the addons, and a subtle BloomNode pass (strength ~0.4, threshold ~1.5) so only emissive things glow (fluorescent coral at night, glowing plankton, sun glints, the octopus' startled flash).
* No external assets. Every texture is drawn on a canvas or generated as pixel data at startup. Every sound is synthesized with WebAudio. The only network requests are three.js from jsDelivr and the Fredoka font from Google Fonts; if the font fails to load, fall back to a system rounded sans-serif without breaking anything.
* Start the HTML with `<!doctype html>` and `<meta charset="utf-8">`.
* It must run inside a sandboxed iframe (`sandbox="allow-scripts allow-pointer-lock"`, no `allow-same-origin`). There, `localStorage` and cookies throw a SecurityError: wrap every storage access in `try/catch` and keep values in memory instead. Do not use `alert`, pop-ups or top-level navigation.
* Neutral tone mapping, soft 2048 shadow map (1024 on phones).
* Known three r170 pitfalls, avoid them:
   * the scene background is drawn after transparent objects, so draw the sky/backdrop as a mesh (or give transparent sky objects `depthWrite: true`), or they disappear;
   * never `.clone()` a CanvasTexture (the clone uploads black); create separate textures or use DataTexture;
   * never let a helper overwrite a shared temp vector that its caller is still using.
* The simulation runs on a fixed 60 Hz timestep and is frame-rate independent. At low frame rates, drop simulation time instead of exploding.
* A quality scaler lowers the pixel ratio, then particle counts, when frames get slow.
* Respect prefers-reduced-motion: softer shake, slower camera moves.

## Priorities

Build in this order and finish each tier properly before the next. A polished tier 1 beats a broken everything.

1. **Must be excellent:** the aquarium block (water volume, caustics, light shafts, surface), the fish school that follows the finger, coral regrowing colour, feeding, the demo mode.
2. **Must work:** the octopus, turtle, shark pass, clownfish and anemone, coral planting, day/night with fluorescence, the reef-alive meter and milestones, sound, the card UI, camera.
3. **Polish:** storm and murky water, the shipwreck and treasure, crabs and seahorse, bubbles tool, glowing plankton trails.

Never ship a feature half-working: if a tier-3 feature can't be done well, leave it out cleanly.

## The diorama

* A 10×7×10 glass aquarium block on a dark wooden stand, with thin white glass edges, soft studio backdrop (deep teal gradient), soft contact shadow.
* **Water:** the whole block is water. The surface is a live wave heightfield (ripples from the finger and from feeding), seen from above and from below (total internal reflection: a silvery mirror from underneath). Volumetric look: blue-green depth fog, **animated caustics** on the sand and on every creature, and **god rays** from the surface that sway.
* **Sea floor:** white sand with ripples, rocks, a sloping reef shelf, seagrass meadow that sways, a sunken shipwreck half-buried at the back.
* **Coral:** procedurally generated branching coral (L-system or recursive cones), table coral, fan coral (sheets that sway), brain coral (sphere with a groove pattern), soft coral that pulses, anemones with swaying tentacles. Each coral has a **health** value: **bleached** corals are white-grey and still; healthy corals are saturated (orange, pink, purple, yellow, teal) and gently move. Health changes animate slowly, colour flowing from the base to the tips.

## Life

* **Fish school (boids):** 150–300 small fish (instanced) with separation, alignment, cohesion and obstacle avoidance (coral, glass, floor). **They follow the pointer** gently when it moves slowly through the water, **scatter** from fast swipes and from the shark, and form a tight **bait ball** when the shark passes. Iridescent silver-blue with a tail wiggle.
* **Reef fish:** a few species with personalities (yellow tangs, striped damselfish, a parrotfish that nibbles coral and leaves tiny sand puffs), each with its own home coral.
* **Clownfish pair** living in an anemone: they dart out to the finger and back, nuzzle into the tentacles.
* **Octopus:** crawls over rocks with curling arms, **changes colour and texture to match what it sits on** (sand, coral, rock), flashes white when poked and **squirts a cloud of ink** then jets away.
* **Sea turtle:** glides through slowly on a loop, sometimes rests on the sand.
* **Reef shark:** passes every ~45 s (or with the Shark button), unhurried; the school balls up and small fish hide in coral.
* **Crabs** scuttle on the sand; a **seahorse** hides in the seagrass (tail curled around a blade).

## Tools (card, keys 1–5)

* **Hand:** move slowly through the water and the school follows; swipe fast to scatter; tap the surface for a ripple; tap a creature to poke it.
* **Feed:** tap to sprinkle food flakes at the surface; they drift down with wobble; fish dart to them (a feeding frenzy with little bites); fed fish make the corals near them healthier.
* **Coral:** tap the reef to plant a new coral fragment (cycle type with repeated taps); it grows over ~10 s with a growth animation.
* **Clean:** brush over bleached coral to remove algae and kick-start recovery (sparkle particles).
* **Bubbles:** place an air stone; a column of bubbles rises and wobbles to the surface (the turtle likes to swim through it).

## Simulation

* Coral health rises with nearby fish activity, feeding and cleaning, and falls slowly in a storm or if the water is murky. Recovery spreads to neighbouring corals.
* **Day / night slider:** at night the light dims to deep blue, corals **fluoresce** (green, pink, orange emissive), plankton glows when disturbed (the finger leaves a sparkling trail), the octopus hunts, the fish sleep in the coral.
* **Storm slider:** surface waves grow, light flickers, sand gets stirred up (murky water) and settles again over time.

## Goal and milestones

* **Reef alive** meter (0–100%): average coral health plus how many species are present. The reef starts **bleached and grey** with few fish; it ends vivid, crowded and moving.
* At 100%: a celebration: every coral blooms bright, a manta ray glides overhead, and the treasure chest in the shipwreck creaks open with a golden glow.

Milestones (toasts, once each): "First feeding", "School follows you", "First coral bloom", "Octopus ink!", "Shark pass", "Night glow", "Turtle visit", "Reef alive".

## Easter egg

When the reef reaches 100% at night, a **whale's eye** slowly slides past the back glass, blinks once, and is gone. Toast: "Something big was watching." Never hint at it in the UI.

## Interface

A light, playful UI that never covers the world. On phones the card becomes a compact bottom sheet.

* Top left:
   * small caps "POKEABLE · WORLD";
   * a big chunky rounded heading on two lines, "Coral" / "Reef", in Fredoka from Google Fonts, dark ink by day and light at night, with a tiny bubble rising from the "o";
   * caption "Bring the reef back to life.".
* Top right: a live status dot with "WEBGPU · LIVE" (or "WEBGL2 · LIVE"), a speaker pill button (ON / MUTED), and "PAUSED" when paused.
* Right card "Reef": about 240 px wide, off-white, 20 px corners, soft shadow, no hairlines, coral-pink (#f2667a) accent, collapsible to a small pill. Contents:
   * a big animated "Reef alive" % with a bar, and species icons (fish, clownfish, octopus, turtle, seahorse) that light up when seen
   * tool picker: Hand, Feed, Coral, Clean, Bubbles, each with a drawn icon and its key number
   * event buttons: Shark, Feeding time
   * sliders with monospace value chips: Time of day, Storm, School size, Sound (master volume)
   * switches: Fish (on), Caustics (on), Slow motion (¼ speed), Cinema
   * buttons Reset and New (random seed), a dark full-width Pause/Resume pill, and the world's number ("No. 0001").
* Bottom left: a one-line hint that changes with the tool:
   * Hand: "Move slowly. The fish will follow you."
   * Feed: "Tap the surface to feed."
   * Coral: "Tap the reef to plant coral."
   * Clean: "Brush the white coral back to life."
   * Bubbles: "Place an air stone."
* Bottom right: a collapsible "How it works" panel, 5–6 plain lines on the boids school, coral health and recovery, caustics and light, day and night fluorescence, the camera controls, and synthesized sound.
* Toasts at the top centre for milestones and events.
* Keys: 1–5 tools, K shark, F feeding time, Space pause, R reset, N new, M mute, S slow motion, C cinema, 0 reset view, Esc stop follow / exit cinema.

## Camera

* OrbitControls with damping and zoom to cursor, within sensible limits.
* Double-click the turtle, the octopus or the shark to follow it; Esc or 0 stops.
* Camera bar (floating pill, bottom right of the scene area): zoom −, a zoom % readout, zoom +, rotate left, rotate right, reset; button moves tween smoothly.
* The default framing fits the whole world into the free area, accounting for the card and title.
* **Cinema (`C`):** hides all UI and slowly orbits the camera.

## Sound

* WebAudio only. Create the AudioContext on the first gesture and never before.
* Master gain feeds a compressor, so rapid actions never clip. Limit voices (about 16) and wrap every call in try/catch so a failing audio call never breaks the world.
* Loops: soft underwater ambience (low filtered noise with slow swells), gentle bubbling, storm rumble with the Storm slider, a dreamy pad at night.
* One-shots: swishes for the school turning, nibble ticks when fish eat, plop for food flakes, a bubbly burst for ink, a deep slow whoosh for the shark, crackle of a coral blooming, a soft chime for each milestone, a deep whale call for the Easter egg.

## Demo mode (required)

If the URL has `?demo=1` (or `#demo`), auto-play a deterministic 4.0 s loop:

* Rules:
   * Hide all UI and the cursor; never create an AudioContext.
   * Fixed quality, default seed, the reef already half alive (some bleached corals, a healthy school), default camera, no OrbitControls.
   * Drive the simulation from real elapsed time with the fixed timestep, and restart from the identical state every 4.0 s.
   * Start moving within 1 s of load, and stay readable at 15 fps.
* Timeline:
   * 0.0–1.2 s: the school sweeps through the frame in an S-curve following an invisible finger; light rays sway.
   * 1.2–2.2 s: food flakes drift down; the school bursts into a feeding frenzy.
   * 2.2–3.2 s: a bleached coral in front recovers: colour flows from the base to the tips; the octopus flashes colour on a rock.
   * 3.2–4.0 s: the turtle glides through; the school regroups.

## Before you finish, check

* The school follows the slow finger, scatters from fast swipes and balls up for the shark, never passing through coral, floor or glass.
* Feeding, planting, cleaning and coral recovery all work and spread.
* Octopus colour matching and ink; turtle, shark, clownfish, crabs, seahorse.
* Day/night fluorescence and plankton trails; storm and murky water settling.
* Reaching 100%: the celebration and the Easter egg at night.
* Every tool, slider, switch, button and key; follow mode; Cinema; pause and resume; resizing to phone width.
* Sound behaviour.
* It works inside `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-pointer-lock">` with no errors (storage blocked).
* `?demo=1` matches the timeline.
* No console or WebGPU validation errors, and it stays smooth on a mid-range laptop.

Put the school that follows your finger and the reef regaining colour first. It should be the calmest, most alive thing on the screen.

items.prompt:
Build an interactive 3D “Jelly Koi Pond” in a single self-contained HTML file.

Create a small oval pond made entirely of soft, translucent jelly, floating just above a warm pastel background. Inside the jelly, add colorful koi fish and smooth little pebbles. Place lily pads, pink water lilies, and one adorable green frog with big eyes on the surface.

The pond should look like a beautiful miniature Japanese garden trapped inside a glossy gummy candy. Give it visible thickness, rounded edges, soft reflections, convincing transparency, and a soft shadow underneath.

Make the jelly physically interactive:
- Click and drag any part of the pond to stretch and lift it.
- Deform the pond locally rather than moving it as a rigid object.
- On release, let it bounce and wobble before gradually settling.
- Keep the fish, pebbles, lily pads, flowers, and frog attached to their positions within or on the deforming pond.
- Let the koi swim slowly when the pond is undisturbed.
- Clicking the surface should create a small ripple.

Add a compact, elegant control bar with Drag and Wobble modes, a jelly softness slider, three color options (mint, blue, and pink), and a reset button.

Use a minimal editorial layout with a large serif “Jelly Koi Pond.” title in the upper-left corner, small interaction hints, generous whitespace, and a soft sage background. Keep the pond as the main focus.

Use procedural geometry and materials, with no external image or model assets. Include lighting, shadows, mouse and touch support, and responsive resizing. Keep the simulation stable during strong dragging and repeated interactions.

Deliver a complete working experience, not a static mockup.
